q: Symmetry, geometric layouts, a strong central axis, and clipped topiary hedges asserting control over nature — as seen at Versailles — describe which garden type?
o: Tropical Gardens
Formal Gardens
Japanese Zen Gardens
Informal Gardens
n: Formal Gardens are characterized by symmetry, geometric shapes, and a clear central axis. They use clipped hedges (topiary) and precise paths to demonstrate human control over nature. Example: Versailles Gardens, France — displaying power and control through monumental landscape design.

q: Adding color, form, texture, and fragrance to a landscape fulfills which functional purpose of softscape?
o: Ecological Benefits
Aesthetic Beauty
Structural Support
Mood & Atmosphere
n: Aesthetic Beauty adds color, form, texture, and fragrance.

q: A narrow trunk that widens into its canopy (e.g., Crape Myrtle), offering moderate shade suited to small plantings, describes which tree shape?
o: Pyramidal/Conical
Vase-shaped
Round/Spreading
Oval/Umbrella
n: The Vase-shaped tree has a narrow trunk widening into the canopy (e.g., Crape Myrtle), giving moderate shade good for small gardens and plantings.

q: What is the main function that retaining walls serve?
o: To mark property lines and screen views for privacy
To hold back soil and make level terraces on slopes
To give filtered shade and a vertical design anchor
To separate garden beds from lawn and keep them neat
n: Retaining walls hold back soil, especially on sloped landscapes, and create level terraces for planting or entertaining. They also add vertical dimension and visual interest, and can double as informal seating or raised garden beds.

q: What natural benefit comes from fallen leaves?
o: They permanently damage the landscape's hardscape
They create natural mulch, returning nutrients to the soil
They eliminate the need for any soil at all
They prevent all future plant growth
n: Falling leaves create natural mulch, returning nutrients to the soil.

q: Landscaped areas are said to be especially valuable for building healing environments in which settings?
o: Parking garages and industrial sites
Hospitals and schools
Warehouses and factories
Highways and overpasses
n: Landscaping creates healing environments especially in hospitals and schools, where landscaped areas provide restorative spaces.

q: Which garden type makes water the central design and ecological feature, as seen in Monet's garden at Giverny?
o: Japanese Zen Gardens
Water Gardens
Informal Gardens
Botanical Gardens
n: Water Gardens highlight water as the central design and ecological element, using ponds, aquatic plants, and fish (koi). Example: Giverny — Monet's Water Garden, inspired by his famous Water Lilies series, blending water and floral beauty.

q: Which of the following is the correct definition of UNITY as a landscape design principle?
o: Distributing visual weight evenly across a space
Achieving harmony by using consistent elements and themes throughout the landscape
Drawing attention to a specific area using a distinctive feature
Ensuring the size of elements relates appropriately to each other
n: Unity is achieving harmony by using consistent elements and themes throughout the landscape.

q: How is SIMPLICITY defined in landscape design?
o: Ensuring elements relate appropriately in size
Creating movement and flow through repetition
Avoiding clutter by keeping the design clean and intentional
Distributing visual weight evenly
n: Simplicity is avoiding clutter by keeping the design clean and intentional.

q: In tropical climates, which type of tree should be favored to handle year-round heat and UV exposure?
o: Deciduous trees only
Ornamental trees only
Dense evergreen trees
Fruit-bearing trees only
n: Tropical climates: opt for dense evergreen trees to manage year-round heat and UV exposure.

q: What role do edging and borders play in a landscape design?
o: To give filtered shade and a vertical anchor to a garden
To separate zones, like beds from lawn, and keep edges neat
To hold back soil and make level terraces on a slope
To guide people along the main circulation routes
n: Edging and Borders separate different landscape zones (e.g., garden beds from grass) and maintain neatness.

q: Which set of materials is typically associated with hardscape?
o: Soil, compost, mulch and bark chips
Stone, concrete, wood, metal and brick
Trees, shrubs, flowers and vines
Turf, groundcovers, mosses and ferns
n: Hardscape materials include stone, concrete, wood, metal, bricks, tiles, and gravel.

q: Which garden type looks natural yet is carefully planned, with winding paths, irregular tree clusters, and hidden views meant to evoke a romantic countryside?
o: Water Gardens
Informal Gardens
Formal Gardens
Botanical Gardens
n: Informal Gardens are designed to look natural but are highly planned. They feature winding paths, irregular clumps of trees, and hidden vistas to mimic a romanticized countryside, encouraging exploration and a sense of discovery.

q: How is softscape defined in landscape design?
o: The non-living, man-made elements of a landscape
The lighting and sound systems of an outdoor space
All the living parts: plants, soil, turf and mulch
The paving, walls and structures that frame a garden
n: Softscape refers to all the living components of a landscape — the plants, soil, turf, and other organic materials. These elements breathe life into a space and are typically dynamic, changing with the seasons, growing over time, and requiring active maintenance.

q: Which of these is a genuine challenge associated with softscape?
o: Poor drainage that makes water pool on paved surfaces
Climate, pests and disease; it needs seasonal replanting
High cost and the risk of looking sterile and cold
It cannot be combined with walls, decks or paving
n: Challenges of softscape include that it requires consistent care (watering, pruning, fertilizing), may be affected by climate, pests, or diseases, and needs seasonal planning and replacement.

q: How does landscaping soften a building's hard edges?
o: Removing trees near the building so its lines read clearly
Adding paved terraces that extend the building outward
Organic forms contrast with and balance sharp building lines
Painting the building in earth tones to match the plants
n: Landscaping softens hard edges: organic elements contrast and balance sharp building lines and materials like concrete or glass.

q: Which statement correctly characterizes deciduous trees?
o: They have a single unbranched stem and a crown of fronds
They remain evergreen year-round with needle-like leaves
They are chosen primarily for their flowers rather than shade
They have a seasonal cycle, shedding all their leaves for part of the year
n: Deciduous Trees are characterized by their seasonal cycle, shedding all their leaves for part of the year.

q: How do broad leaves compare with small or needle-like leaves in terms of shading?
o: Both provide identical shading effects
Broad leaves offer only dappled light, while needle-like leaves block all sunlight
Broad leaves block more sunlight, while small or needle-like leaves offer dappled or filtered light
Neither leaf type affects shading
n: Broad leaves block more sunlight. Small or needle-like leaves offer dappled or filtered light.

q: Which group of items falls under softscape's 'living materials'?
o: Stone, concrete, gravel and pavers
Fences, decks, pergolas and gazebos
Trees, shrubs, flowers, grass and vines
Soil, compost, mulch and bark chips
n: Living materials in softscape include trees, shrubs, flowers, grass, vines, groundcovers, and mosses.

q: Tall, narrow trees (e.g., Italian Cypress, Palms) that give limited shade but strong vertical framing, ideal for borders and walkway lining, exemplify which tree shape?
o: Weeping
Columnar
Irregular/Natural
Vase-shaped
n: The Columnar shape is tall and narrow (e.g., Italian Cypress, Palms), providing limited shade but useful for vertical framing; best used for borders and lining walkways.

q: How does the seasonal behavior of deciduous trees differ from that of evergreens with respect to sun shading?
o: Both behave identically across seasons
Deciduous trees allow passive heating during colder months, while evergreens are consistent blockers
Evergreens shed their needles in winter to allow passive heating
Deciduous trees block all sunlight year-round, while evergreens allow full sun in winter
n: Seasonal Behavior: Deciduous trees allow passive heating during colder months; evergreens are consistent blockers.

q: A triangular, cone-shaped tree (e.g., Pine, Spruce) that shades lower levels but has a narrower canopy, best suited for windbreaks and backdrops, describes which shape?
o: Vase-shaped
Round/Spreading
Pyramidal/Conical
Oval/Umbrella
n: The Pyramidal/Conical shape is triangular or cone-shaped (e.g., Pine, Spruce), giving shade at lower levels but with a less broad canopy; best used for windbreaks and backdrops.

q: Which statement best describes softscape's role in the environment?
o: It has no impact on stormwater or air quality
It prevents any wildlife from entering a landscape
It absorbs water, purifies air, provides shade, attracts wildlife, and helps cool the environment
It only provides a visual focal point with no ecological function
n: Softscape's environmental role includes purifying air, absorbing water, providing shade, attracting wildlife (birds, bees, butterflies), and helping cool the environment.

q: In terms of height and branch spread, what shading roles do taller versus wider trees typically play?
o: Height and spread have no bearing on shade coverage
Taller trees offer overhead shade, while wide trees provide lateral coverage
Taller trees provide no shade, while wide trees offer only overhead shade
Both taller and wider trees serve identical shading roles
n: Taller trees offer overhead shade; wide trees provide lateral coverage.

q: How do softscapes change over time, according to the discussion of seasonality?
o: They stay the same size and look all year
They bloom, shed and fill out over time
They change only when watered by hand
They lose their function once planted
n: Softscapes evolve with time — blooming, shedding leaves, growing fuller, or thinning out.

q: Downward-drooping branches (e.g., Weeping Willow) that create diffused shade and dramatic ambiance, well-suited near water features or meditative spaces, describe which tree shape?
o: Columnar
Irregular/Natural
Weeping
Round/Spreading
n: The Weeping tree shape has downward drooping branches (e.g., Weeping Willow), giving diffused shade and adding dramatic ambiance; best used near water features or meditative spaces.

q: How does landscaping help buffer noise?
o: Water features mask every kind of outside noise alone
Plants and earth berms absorb and block street noise
Hard walls reflect noise back so no plants are needed
Lawns spread out the sound so it fades before the house
n: Noise Buffering: plants and earth berms reduce noise pollution from streets or neighboring properties.

q: What does thicker foliage generally provide in terms of canopy density and shading?
o: Lighter, dappled shade that lets in more sun
Shade only in the cooler months of the year
Denser shade, as with Narra, Acacia and Mango
No real change in how well a tree shades
n: Canopy Density: thicker foliage means better shade. Narra, Acacia, and Mango are excellent examples in tropical climates.

q: What is the purpose of structural and decorative features like pergolas, gazebos, benches, statues, and planters?
o: To hold back soil on sloping parts of the site
To add style, give support or mark focal points
To filter air and manage stormwater runoff
To guide cars into driveways and parking areas
n: Structural and Decorative Elements enhance style, provide support, or emphasize focal points in the landscape.

q: Botanically speaking, what characterizes palm trees?
o: Dicots with a branching trunk and a broad leafy canopy
Monocots with one unbranched stem and a crown of fronds
Needle-leaved conifers that bear their seeds in cones
Deciduous trees that drop all their fronds each year
n: Palm Trees are monocots (flowering plants whose seeds contain only one embryonic leaf, or cotyledon), often featuring a single unbranched stem and a crown of fronds. They are the hallmark of tropical and subtropical site design.

q: As a hardscape element, what do pathways and walkways primarily accomplish?
o: To mark property lines and give privacy screening
To hold back soil and make level terraces on slopes
To guide movement and define circulation routes
To give a sensory focal point and a calm mood
n: Pathways and walkways guide movement, create flow, and define circulation routes throughout a landscape.

q: Which of these is a genuine key characteristic of a garden?
o: It must always follow a formal, symmetrical layout
It is artistic and botanical, arranged around a theme
It needs no regular care once it is fully planted
It must be open to the public for free at all times
n: Key Characteristics of a garden include being artistic and botanical in nature, carefully arranged with themes (color, plant species, symmetry), and being more personal, intimate, and contemplative; gardens sometimes serve scientific or educational purposes.

q: How is SCALE defined in landscape design?
o: Water features, rustling plants, or birds enhancing ambiance
The layout and open/closed feeling of an area, and how areas are connected
The relative size of landscape components to human scale and other elements
Natural or artificial lighting to highlight features and ensure safety
n: Scale is the relative size of landscape components to human scale and other elements.

q: How is hardscape defined in landscape design?
o: The living parts: plants, soil, turf and mulch
The non-living, man-made elements that give structure
The irrigation and drainage pipes under a garden
The seasonal color scheme of the flowering plants
n: Hardscape involves the non-living, solid, and man-made elements of the landscape. These give structure, stability, and function to outdoor areas, forming the framework where softscape elements are arranged.

q: Which edging material is noted for being minimalist and long-lasting?
o: Gravel Borders
Brick or Stone Borders
Metal Edging
Concrete Curbs
n: Metal Edging is minimalist and long-lasting.

q: Landscaping is described as integral to which pair of green building certifications?
o: ISO and OSHA
IBC and NFPA
LEED and BERDE
ASTM and ANSI
n: Sustainable Architecture: Landscaping is integral to green building certifications like LEED and BERDE.

q: Which garden type is defined by lush, varied vegetation from dense planting and a naturalistic layout, as seen at the Baguio Botanical Garden?
o: Formal Gardens
Tropical Gardens
Water Gardens
Japanese Zen Gardens
n: Tropical Gardens showcase lush, diverse vegetation through dense planting, a naturalistic layout, and exotic species. Example: Baguio Botanical Garden — highlighting native Cordillera plants and traditional huts.

q: By defining zones such as patios, courtyards, and play areas, what does landscaping achieve, per the discussion of functional space extension?
o: Wayfinding and circulation for visitors
'Outdoor rooms' that extend living space
A higher resale value for the property
Buffering of noise from nearby streets
n: Landscaping can define zones like patios, courtyards, and play areas — extending living or working spaces outdoors as 'Outdoor Rooms.'

q: For passive solar design, broad-leaf deciduous trees should be placed on which sides of a building to block the most intense afternoon sun?
o: North and East sides of a building
Directly against the building's foundation
South and West sides of a building
Only in interior courtyards
n: Broad-leaf deciduous trees should be placed on the South and West sides of a building to block the most intense afternoon sun.

q: Which pathway material is noted as affordable and well-suited to rustic or informal gardens?
o: Stone Pavers
Concrete Paths
Brick Walkways
Gravel Trails
n: Gravel Trails are affordable and ideal for rustic or informal gardens.

q: Which functional purpose of hardscape describes its role as a focal point or design anchor?
o: Usability
Visual Anchor
Accessibility & Flow
Structural Support
n: Visual Anchor: hardscapes often serve as focal points or design anchors.

q: Which softscape purpose is demonstrated when different planting styles, such as tropical versus zen gardens, evoke distinct emotional responses?
o: Structural Support
Mood & Atmosphere
Ecological Benefits
Aesthetic Beauty
n: Mood & Atmosphere: different planting styles (e.g., tropical vs. zen garden) evoke different emotions and experiences.

q: How is SOUND defined in landscape design?
o: Using differences in color, texture, and shape to add interest
Distributing visual weight evenly across a space
Water features, rustling plants, or birds that can enhance ambiance
The layout and open/closed feeling of an area
n: Sound refers to water features, rustling plants, or birds, which can enhance ambiance.

q: Compared to deciduous trees, what kind of shade do palms cast, and how should they mainly be used?
o: No shade whatsoever; purely structural support
Dappled or minimal shade; primarily for aesthetic framing rather than passive cooling of large facades
Only shade during the dry season
Dense, complete shade; as the primary passive cooling strategy for large facades
n: Unlike deciduous trees, palms provide 'dappled' or minimal shade. They should be used for aesthetic framing rather than as a primary strategy for passive cooling of large facades; they are often more effective when planted in naturalistic clusters rather than as single, isolated stalks.

q: What role do fences and screens play as a hardscape feature?
o: To give a sensory focal point with moving water and sound
To hold back soil and make level terraces on a slope
To mark boundaries, give privacy and block views or wind
To guide cars into driveways and parking areas on site
n: Fences and screens define property boundaries, ensure privacy, and block unwanted views or wind; they can also reduce noise pollution when lined with dense vegetation or sound-absorbing panels.

q: How does landscaping contribute to Low-impact Development?
o: By using only imported, non-native plant species
By replacing all softscape with hardscape
Native and drought-resistant plants reduce water use and maintenance
By requiring high water use and heavy maintenance
n: Landscaping supports Low-impact Development: native and drought-resistant plants reduce water use and maintenance.

q: Which type of balance in landscape design is described as 'formal'?
o: Proportional Balance
Asymmetrical Balance
Rhythmic Balance
Symmetrical Balance
n: Symmetrical Balance is formal, distributing visual weight evenly on both sides of an axis.

q: For south-facing areas, which trees are recommended for seasonal light control — shading in summer and admitting sun in winter?
o: Coniferous/evergreen trees
Palm trees only
Deciduous trees
Vine-covered trellises only
n: South-facing areas: use deciduous trees for seasonal control (shade in summer, sun in winter).

q: Given their year-round density, what role do coniferous/evergreen trees primarily serve?
o: Edible fruit for an edible landscape
Light, dappled shade for lawns and patios
Windbreaks that cut wind speed all year
A short burst of color in the flowering season
n: Because they remain dense throughout the year, coniferous/evergreen trees are the primary tool for creating windbreaks. They can reduce wind speed significantly, lowering heating costs in winter, and their year-round density makes them ideal for screening unsightly views or dampening noise.

q: What drawback do ornamental trees present once their flowering period is over?
o: They stop absorbing carbon dioxide
They may look 'skeletal' or sparse for the rest of the year
They become hazardous to walk beneath
They immediately die and must be replaced
n: An ornamental tree that looks stunning for two weeks of flowering might look 'skeletal' or sparse for the rest of the year. Some also shed fine, needle-like leaves that can clog drainage systems or pool filters more easily than larger leaves.

q: Unstructured, wild growth (e.g., Wild Guava), with shade that varies unevenly but reads as rustic, best suited to forested or naturalistic settings, describes which tree shape?
o: Weeping
Irregular/Natural
Pyramidal/Conical
Columnar
n: The Irregular/Natural shape shows unstructured or wild growth (e.g., Wild Guava); shade varies by size and may be uneven but rustic, best used in forested settings and naturalistic gardens.

q: Called the 'lungs of the city' and vital to physical and mental health, which park type is exemplified by Central Park in New York City?
o: Theme Parks
Urban Parks
National Parks
Pocket Parks
n: Urban Parks are multifunctional green spaces within a high-density city, functioning as the 'lungs of the city' and essential for physical and mental health. Example: Central Park, NYC — a model of landscape architecture combining lakes, meadows, trails, and performance spaces within a bustling city.

q: How is RHYTHM defined in landscape design?
o: Avoiding clutter by keeping the design clean and intentional
The layout and open/closed feeling of an area
Creating movement and flow by repeating elements like plants, colors, or paths
The relative size of landscape components to human scale
n: Rhythm is creating movement and flow by repeating elements like plants, colors, or paths.

q: Why are palm trees well suited to tight urban spaces or planting near foundations and sidewalks?
o: Their deep taproots anchor them far below the foundations
They need little sun, so they grow well between buildings
Most have small, non-invasive root balls and narrow trunks
Their wide canopies shade the sidewalk and the building
n: Most palms have relatively small, non-invasive root balls and narrow trunks, making them ideal for tight urban spaces or planting near foundations and sidewalks.

q: In landscape architecture, what function do design principles serve?
o: A list of native Philippine plant species approved for use
A checklist of documents needed for a construction permit
Guidelines for pleasing, functional, sustainable outdoor spaces
A method of pricing hardscape materials and installation
n: The principles in landscape design serve as guidelines to create aesthetically pleasing, functional, and sustainable outdoor spaces.

q: Roughly how far apart should large trees be spaced, depending on canopy spread?
o: 50-75 feet apart
1-5 feet apart
15-30 feet apart
100+ feet apart
n: Large trees should be spaced 15–30 feet apart, depending on canopy spread.

q: Under aesthetic enhancement, how does landscaping achieve visual harmony?
o: By using only one plant species throughout the site
By complementing the architectural style of the building
By screening the building from view with dense planting
By contrasting sharply with every line of the building
n: Landscaping creates visual harmony by complementing the architectural style (modern, tropical, minimalist, classical).

q: How is SPACE defined in landscape design?
o: Distributing visual weight evenly
The layout and open/closed feeling of the area, and also how areas are connected
The relative size of landscape components to human scale
Natural or artificial lighting to highlight features
n: Space is the layout and open/closed feeling of the area; also how areas are connected.

q: Which pathway material is described as popular for gardens or residential yards, valued for being natural and textured?
o: Gravel Trails
Brick Walkways
Concrete Paths
Stone Pavers
n: Stone Pavers are popular in gardens or residential yards, and are natural and textured.

q: What role do water features serve in landscape design?
o: To guide movement through paths, stairs, and ramps
To enhance sensory experience, promote tranquility, and serve as a visual centerpiece
To hold back soil on sloped landscapes
To separate different landscape zones and maintain neatness
n: Water features enhance sensory experience, promote tranquility, and serve as a visual centerpiece. They balance the solidity of the landscape with movement and reflection.

q: Under environmental benefits, how does landscaping improve air quality?
o: Plants release pollutants into the air
Hardscape elements filter airborne particulates
Landscaping has no effect on air quality
Plants absorb pollutants and release oxygen
n: Landscaping improves air quality: plants absorb pollutants and release oxygen.

q: Beyond cost and the risk of overwhelming a design, what other challenge does hardscape pose?
o: It needs seasonal replanting like trees and flower beds
It needs drainage planning to avoid pooling and flooding
It is affected by pests and plant diseases each year
It cannot be combined with trees and planted areas
n: Hardscape needs proper drainage and surface planning to avoid water pooling or flooding.

q: Which structural feature offers filtered shade along with a vertical design anchor?
o: Statues, Columns, and Planters
Pergolas and Gazebos
Edging
Benches and Seating Walls
n: Pergolas and Gazebos provide filtered shade and a vertical design anchor.

q: Guiding movement through paths, stairs, and ramps describes which functional purpose of hardscape?
o: Structural Support
Accessibility & Flow
Usability
Visual Anchor
n: Accessibility & Flow guides movement through paths, stairs, and ramps.

q: Focused on plant conservation, education, and display — as at the Singapore Botanic Gardens — which garden type is this?
o: Water Gardens
Tropical Gardens
Formal Gardens
Botanical Gardens
n: Botanical Gardens are purposed for plant conservation, education, and display, using design elements like scientific plant labeling, arboretums, and thematic zones. Example: Singapore Botanic Gardens, a World Heritage site with an orchid garden and rainforest trail.

q: Ornamental/flowering trees are chosen mainly for what quality?
o: Their ability to act as dense year-round windbreaks
Their yield of fruit for an edible landscape design
Their looks: flowers, leaf color, bark or canopy shape
Their root systems that hold soil against erosion
n: Ornamental trees are chosen primarily for their aesthetic qualities — flowers, foliage color, bark texture, or unique canopy shapes. They are used primarily for decorative value and sometimes partial shading.

q: What distinguishes a deck from a patio?
o: Decks are raised and of wood; patios are at grade in stone or concrete
Patios are raised and of wood; decks are at grade in stone or concrete
Decks are always roofed; patios are always open to the sky above
Decks are for public parks; patios are only for private homes
n: Decks are typically elevated and made of wood or composite materials, while patios are ground-level and made from stone, brick, or concrete.

q: For driveways or walkways, which tree shapes are best to avoid obstructing the path?
o: Round/spreading trees
Columnar or vase-shaped trees
Weeping trees
Irregular/natural trees
n: Driveways or walkways: use columnar or vase-shaped trees to avoid blocking paths.

q: Which decorative patio option mimics stone or brick at a lower cost while offering high design flexibility?
o: Wooden Decks
Gravel Patios
Stamped Concrete Patios
Stone or Tile Patios
n: Stamped Concrete Patios imitate stone or brick at a lower cost with high design flexibility.

q: Beyond framing the planting, what else does hardscape shape?
o: The botanical classification of the plants used on the site
How a space works, how people move and how inviting it feels
The zoning rules and setbacks that apply to the property
The seasonal color changes of the trees and flower beds
n: Hardscape is not just the 'frame' for landscaping — it defines how a space works, how people move through it, and how comfortable, inviting, and expressive it can be.

q: What adaptation lets many palm species withstand high-wind events such as typhoons?
o: By growing exclusively underground
Through flexible trunks and aerodynamic fronds
Through extremely rigid, inflexible trunks
By shedding all fronds permanently
n: Many palm species have evolved to survive high-wind events (like typhoons) due to their flexible trunks and aerodynamic fronds.

q: Dome-shaped on top and slightly taller than wide (e.g., Mango, Rain Tree), giving strong overhead shade but less horizontal spread — best for driveways and patios — describes which tree shape?
o: Vase-shaped
Oval/Umbrella
Round/Spreading
Pyramidal/Conical
n: The Oval/Umbrella shape is dome-like on top, slightly taller than wide (e.g., Mango, Rain Tree), giving good overhead shade with less horizontal coverage; best used for driveways and patios.

q: How is EMPHASIS (Focal Point) defined in landscape design?
o: Spreading visual weight evenly across the whole space
Drawing the eye to one feature, like a sculpture or tree
Using the same elements and theme throughout the site
Using differences in color, texture and shape for interest
n: Emphasis (Focal Point) is drawing attention to specific areas using distinctive features like a sculpture, fountain, or tree.

q: How is a garden best defined?
o: A protected tract of land managed by the government for its natural state
A cultivated area focused on plants and beauty, often with symbolic meaning
A large public area planned for recreation, sports and community events
A small vacant lot in a dense city block turned into a micro-retreat
n: A garden is an intentionally cultivated area primarily focused on plants, aesthetics, and beauty. Gardens can be private or public, and their design often carries symbolic, cultural, or meditative meaning.

q: Which of these is a deciduous tree?
o: Palm
Narra
Pine
Podocarpus
n: Examples of Deciduous Trees include Maple, Oak, Narra, Mahogany, and Acacia.

q: Focused on spiritual contemplation through dry elements like raked sand (symbolizing water) and placed rocks (symbolizing mountains) — as at Ryoan-ji in Kyoto — which garden type is this?
o: Formal Gardens
Water Gardens
Tropical Gardens
Japanese Zen Gardens
n: Japanese Zen Gardens are focused on spiritual contemplation, using dry elements like raked sand (representing water) and carefully placed rocks (representing mountains). Their purpose is meditation, reflection, and Zen Buddhism. Example: Ryoan-ji Garden, Kyoto — a world-renowned dry landscape garden meant for contemplation.

q: Under climate control and thermal comfort, how do trees and pergolas reduce the need for air conditioning?
o: Leaves reflect the sun back to the sky from the roof surface
Shade cuts heat gain and cools the air around the building
Roots draw heat out of the ground floor slab into the soil
Branches block the wind so that hot air stays away outside
n: Trees and pergolas provide shade, reducing heat gain, lowering surrounding temperatures, and minimizing the need for air conditioning.

q: Retaining walls that prevent soil erosion and pergolas that provide shade illustrate which functional purpose of hardscape?
o: Usability
Accessibility & Flow
Structural Support
Visual Anchor
n: Structural Support: retaining walls prevent soil erosion; pergolas provide shade.

q: Which pathway material is described as classic and patterned, often found in colonial or traditional settings?
o: Gravel Trails
Brick Walkways
Stone Pavers
Concrete Paths
n: Brick Walkways are classic, patterned paths often used in colonial or traditional settings.

q: As illustrated by rough bark versus soft grass, what does TEXTURE refer to among landscape design elements?
o: Sets mood and visual interest
The shape of plants and structures
The surface quality of materials or plants
Defines edges and guides movement
n: Texture is the surface quality of materials or plants (e.g., rough bark vs. soft grass).

q: Among the key elements of landscape design, what does FORM refer to?
o: Surface quality of materials or plants, e.g., rough bark vs. soft grass
Defining edges and guiding movement
The shape of plants and structures, e.g., columnar trees, rounded shrubs
Sets mood and visual interest, impacting seasonal appeal
n: Form is the shape of plants and structures (e.g., columnar trees, rounded shrubs).

q: What maintenance issue is typical of fruit-bearing trees such as Mango?
o: Their roots lift sidewalks and crack foundations
Fallen fruit stains paving and cars and draws pests
Their canopies drop all their leaves each dry season
They need daily watering to set any fruit at all
n: Fruit drop can stain concrete, tiles, and parked cars. High-fructose fruit (like Mango) attracts ants, flies, and rodents if not harvested. Many fruit trees also have aggressive, thirsty root systems that can crack nearby foundations or sidewalks, so they are best kept in 'soft' areas away from high-traffic paths and parking.

q: Aside from plants themselves, what organic components fall under softscape?
o: Bricks and gravel
Concrete and stone
Soil types, compost, and mulch
Metal edging and curbs
n: Organic components of softscape include not just the plants, but also soil types, compost, and mulch.

q: Which driveway/parking hardscape material is textured and slip-resistant?
o: Permeable Pavers
Cobblestone Drives
Exposed Aggregate Concrete
Stamped Concrete
n: Exposed Aggregate Concrete is textured and slip-resistant.

q: Roughly how much can good landscaping raise a property's value?
n: A well-landscaped property can boost value by up to 15–20%.

q: Which driveway material lets water seep through, supporting sustainability?
o: Cobblestone Drives
Exposed Aggregate Concrete
Gravel Trails
Permeable Pavers
n: Permeable Pavers allow water to seep through, supporting sustainability.

q: Which fence type uses trellises or lattices to support climbing plants like bougainvillea or jasmine?
o: Wooden Fences
Concrete Fences
Living Screens (with hard frames)
Metal or Wrought Iron Fences
n: Living Screens (with hard frames) are trellises or lattices that support climbing plants like bougainvillea or jasmine.

q: How is BALANCE defined in landscape design?
o: Avoiding clutter by keeping the design clean and intentional
Using differences in color, texture, and shape to add interest
Creating movement and flow by repeating elements like plants, colors, or paths
Distributing visual weight evenly, which can be symmetrical or asymmetrical
n: Balance is distributing visual weight evenly. This can be Symmetrical Balance (formal) or Asymmetrical Balance (informal but still visually stable).

q: Which water feature may contain aquatic plants, koi fish, or lily pads?
o: Waterfalls
Ponds
Fountains
Gabion Walls
n: Ponds may include aquatic plants, koi fish, or lily pads.

q: How is a park best defined?
o: A single vacant lot converted into a small neighborhood garden
A large planned public area for recreation, rest and social life
A dry landscape garden used mainly for quiet meditation
A private cultivated area focused on plants and beauty
n: A park is a large, planned area of land, often managed by the government or a private organization, that is open to the public for recreation, rest, and social engagement. Parks are designed for multipurpose use and integrate both natural and artificial elements.

q: Which of these is a genuine key characteristic of a park?
o: It serves only one fixed use, like a garden
It is inclusive and zoned for many activities
It is open only to paying members and guests
It is planted densely with no open lawn areas
n: Key Characteristics of a park include being inclusive and community-oriented, multi-zoned for various activities (sports, concerts, walking), often part of urban planning to provide green relief in cities, and promoting social equity by offering free public space.

q: Which retaining wall material blends organically into hilly terrain?
o: Gabion Walls
Concrete Blocks
Natural Stone
Stamped Concrete
n: Natural Stone is organic and blends into hilly landscapes.

q: For courtyards and patios, which tree category — such as Rain Trees or Acacias — is recommended for broad canopy coverage?
o: Columnar or vase-shaped trees
Pyramidal conifers only
Weeping trees only
Broad canopy or umbrella trees
n: Courtyards and patios: use broad canopy or umbrella trees like Rain Trees or Acacias.

q: Among landscape design elements, what does LINE refer to?
o: The shape of plants and structures, such as columnar trees or rounded shrubs
Defining edges, guiding movement, and shaping the layout, e.g., pathways or plant borders
The surface quality of materials or plants
Sets mood and visual interest, impacting seasonal appeal
n: Line defines edges, guides movement, and shapes the layout (e.g., pathways, plant borders).

q: Enabling outdoor dining, relaxation, cooking, or entertaining describes which functional purpose of hardscape?
o: Accessibility & Flow
Usability
Visual Anchor
Structural Support
n: Usability allows for outdoor dining, relaxation, cooking, or entertaining.

q: Large tracts of land protected by government for their natural, semi-natural, or developed state — as with the Palawan Underground River Park — describe which park type?
o: Urban Parks
Pocket Parks
National Parks
Theme Parks
n: National Parks are large tracts of land protected by the government for their natural, semi-natural, or developed state, with a function of protecting natural heritage and biodiversity. Example: Palawan Underground River Park, PH — a UNESCO site known for biodiversity and sustainable tourism.

q: What characterizes coniferous/evergreen trees?
o: One unbranched stem topped with a crown of fronds
Needle or scale leaves, cones, and year-round foliage
Broad leaves that are all shed in the dry season
Showy flowers chosen for a short blooming season
n: Coniferous/Evergreen Trees typically have needle-like or scale-like leaves and produce cones. Most are evergreen, meaning they retain their foliage year-round.

q: Which of these is listed as a real challenge of hardscape?
o: It cannot serve as a focal point
It can become too dominant or sterile if not balanced with softscape
It requires no drainage or surface planning
It is generally cheaper to install than softscape
n: Challenges of hardscape include that it is more expensive to install and modify, and it can become too dominant or sterile if not balanced with softscape.

q: Which fruit trees are among the best thermal buffers against tropical heat?
o: Palm or Cypress
Mango or Caimito
Pine or Juniper
Maple or Oak
n: Species like Mango or Star Apple (Caimito) provide some of the thickest, most effective thermal buffers against tropical heat.

q: How is LIGHT defined in landscape design?
o: Creating movement and flow by repeating elements
Natural or artificial lighting to highlight features and ensure safety
Water features, rustling plants, or birds that can enhance ambiance
The relative size of landscape components to human scale
n: Light is natural or artificial lighting used to highlight features and ensure safety.

q: Coniferous/evergreen trees are best suited to which kind of sun-shading role?
o: Shade in summer, sun in the cool months
Framing views with almost no shade
Light, dappled shade over lawns only
Constant year-round shade and screening
n: Coniferous/evergreen trees provide consistent sunshade throughout the year, and are best used for areas needing constant shading or privacy.

q: Which of these is an ornamental (flowering) tree?
o: Podocarpus
Pine
Jacaranda
Mango
n: Examples of ornamental/flowering trees include Cherry Blossom, Jacaranda, Palawan Cherry, and Fire Tree.

q: Which type of landscape balance is described as informal yet still visually stable?
o: Symmetrical Balance
Proportional Balance
Rhythmic Balance
Asymmetrical Balance
n: Asymmetrical Balance is informal but still visually stable, distributing visual weight unevenly yet in equilibrium.

q: A wide, symmetrical canopy (e.g., Narra, Acacia) that provides broad, even shade over large areas describes which tree shape?
o: Oval/Umbrella
Weeping
Columnar
Round/Spreading
n: The Round/Spreading shape has a wide and symmetrical canopy (e.g., Narra, Acacia), giving wide, even shade over large areas; best used for yards, plazas, and parks.

q: Small-scale spaces, often a single vacant lot or corner of a city block, acting as 'micro-retreats' in dense cities, describe which park type?
o: Urban Parks
Pocket Parks
National Parks
Theme Parks
n: Pocket Parks are small-scale spaces often created on a single vacant lot or a small corner of a city block, functioning as micro-retreats in dense cities. Design considerations include efficient use of limited space, low-maintenance plants, and seating.

q: Which of these is listed as a built element of hardscape?
o: Shrubs, flowers, vines and flowering trees
Groundcovers, mosses, turf and ornamental grasses
Soil, compost, mulch and organic amendments
Walkways, patios, retaining walls and pergolas
n: Built elements of hardscape include walkways, patios, retaining walls, pergolas, decks, driveways, fences, fire pits, and water features.

q: What dual role do fruit-bearing trees serve as staples of 'Edible Landscapes'?
o: Privacy and drainage
Shade and food
Screening views and reducing noise
Windbreaking and erosion control
n: Fruit-bearing trees provide fruit and shade, turning a site from a passive space into a productive one — the staples of 'Edible Landscapes.'

q: How is CONTRAST AND VARIETY defined in landscape design?
o: Ensuring the size of elements relates appropriately to each other
Creating movement and flow by repeating elements
Using differences in color, texture, and shape to add interest
Avoiding clutter by keeping the design clean and intentional
n: Contrast and Variety is using differences in color, texture, and shape to add interest.

q: Which softscape purpose supports biodiversity, manages stormwater runoff, and improves air quality?
o: Aesthetic Beauty
Mood & Atmosphere
Ecological Benefits
Visual Anchor
n: Ecological Benefits: supports biodiversity, manages stormwater runoff, and improves air quality.

q: Centered on entertainment and commercial recreation, with design priorities like ride safety and immersive storytelling — as at Magic Kingdom, Walt Disney World — which park type is this?
o: Urban Parks
National Parks
Pocket Parks
Theme Parks
n: Theme Parks function for entertainment and commercial recreation, with design considerations including ride safety, fantasy architecture, and immersive storytelling. Example: Magic Kingdom at Walt Disney World Resort, Florida.

q: How does landscaping help manage stormwater?
o: Wider concrete canals and underground culverts
Paving over lawns so water drains off faster
Raising every building above the flood level
Rain gardens, green roofs and permeable paving
n: Landscaping manages stormwater: rain gardens, green roofs, and permeable surfaces reduce runoff and prevent flooding.

q: Across the seasons in temperate or subtropical climates, what is the typical behavior of deciduous trees?
o: Shade all year; their leaves block the low winter sun as well
Shade in summer; bare branches let winter sun warm the building
No shade in summer; full leaves only during the cold months
Flowers in summer; dense evergreen foliage through winter
n: In temperate or subtropical climates, deciduous trees provide dense canopy shade in summer, reducing solar heat gain on facades; in winter their bare branches allow sunlight to penetrate and naturally warm the building.

q: How is PROPORTION defined in landscape design?
o: Distributing visual weight evenly across the space
Sizes of elements that suit each other and the space
Creating movement by repeating plants or colors
Drawing attention to one area with a strong feature
n: Proportion is ensuring that the size of elements relates appropriately to each other and to the overall space.

q: Metal cages filled with rocks, producing an industrial and rugged look, describe which retaining wall material?
o: Brick
Concrete Blocks
Natural Stone
Gabion Walls
n: Gabion walls are metal cages filled with rocks, giving an industrial and rugged look.

q: Among landscape design elements, what does COLOR refer to?
o: The shape of plants and structures
Sets mood and visual interest, and impacts seasonal appeal
Defining edges and guiding movement
The surface quality of materials or plants
n: Color sets mood and visual interest, and impacts seasonal appeal.

q: How does landscaping help mitigate the Urban Heat Island Effect?
o: Light-colored paving reflects more of the sun back to the sky
More paved parking spreads the heat over a wider area
Green surfaces cool the air by shade and evapotranspiration
Tall buildings cast long shadows over the streets below
n: Landscaping reduces the Urban Heat Island Effect: green surfaces cool the surroundings through evapotranspiration and shade.
